task.title: Execute one provider-requested tool step
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/559 with an additive provider boundary that returns final content or dispatches at most one registered tool request through the existing durable task associated path.
acceptance_criteria: Keep the existing AssistantProvider and tool-free runtime behavior compatible.
Call the tool-capable provider exactly once and dispatch at most one tool with caller-owned task, invocation, registry, store, and authorization inputs.
Return explicit continuation state and exact tool input/output in memory while durable invocation evidence remains metadata-only.
Preserve typed provider, lookup, task, permission, adapter, identity, and persistence failures without retries or an automatic continuation loop.

attempts.summary: Established RED with one-step provider/tool runtime tests.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused tests failed because the additive tool-capable provider response and runtime operation did not exist.
attempts.patch: Kept tests for final content, allowed dispatch, denial, unknown tools, provider and adapter failures, duplicate identity, missing tasks, exact call counts, and metadata-only retention.

attempts.summary: Implemented one bounded provider/tool response dispatch.
attempts.diagnostic: The provider is called once; final content returns directly, while one tool request reuses ToolRegistry::invoke_for_task_durable and returns ProviderRequired without a second provider call.
attempts.patch: Added the provider-neutral response, explicit step outcome and continuation types, typed wrapper errors, focused integration coverage, and behavior documentation.

attempts.summary: Fixed a missing continuation value found by independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: The first continuation shape retained exact output but omitted the exact tool input needed for a later provider continuation.
attempts.patch: Added a failing assertion, retained the exact input alongside output in memory, and re-reviewed with no remaining blocking finding.

attempts.summary: Verified and merged the bounded runtime slice.
attempts.diagnostic: Pinned just verify and independent pre-commit review passed. GitHub Rust quality gate run 30131438736 succeeded; CodeRabbit reported adaptive review limiting rather than a substantive review.
attempts.patch: Pull request 560 squash-merged as 2ee721dbccdd01231804aa897541891277bbaa6d and closed issue 559.

outcome.summary: A tool-capable provider can now produce final content or request one durably evidenced, task associated tool invocation with explicit caller-owned continuation.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test provider_tool_runtime
Independent pre-commit review # exact tool input omission fixed and re-review passed

lessons: Compose provider dispatch with the established durable registry path instead of duplicating permission and persistence semantics.
A continuation must retain both exact tool input and output in memory even when durable policy intentionally retains metadata only.
One provider call and at most one tool call form a testable boundary before any automatic runtime loop is introduced.
A green review status explicitly marked rate limited is evidence of no substantive review and must not be represented otherwise.
